_comment: Review deck for the page start-session feature (app commit b83b8af3e).
Pictures are real screenshots of an isolated dev window (throwaway HOME, own profile), driven with explore + real mouse clicks, 2026-10-14.
Each Approve slide shows two moments of the flow as its before/after pair (labels name them). Shot in Midnight only.
The last slide is review finding F4 (page-start-session.code-review.md) as a Question.
title: Pages can open a new conversation — keep it?

steps.path: Pages, then Frontier Lab, the first time you open it
steps.headline: The first time, Frontier Lab asks once whether it may open a new-conversation window, then loads.
steps.changed: The usual approval card gains one line: the page may open a new-conversation window with a message it writes. Allow and open loads the page.
steps.notice: You answer this card once per page. Not now leaves the page closed.
steps.risk: The card says you'll see the message before anything is sent. You do, but only in the chat box after you press Create Session (see the last slide).

steps.path: Frontier Lab, the Update now button at the top right
steps.headline: Update now opens the normal new-conversation window, with the Frontier project already picked.
steps.changed: Before this, Update now showed a box with the message to copy and paste. Now it opens the same window as New Session, titled Start a conversation, From Frontier Lab.
steps.notice: The project is already Frontier. You still choose the model and the permission switch, and nothing has been sent.
steps.risk: The window does not show the message itself. You first see it in the chat box after Create Session.

steps.path: The new-conversation window, then Create Session
steps.headline: Create Session opens the chat with the weekly-update request waiting in the message box, not sent.
steps.changed: The message box is filled with "Run the Frontier Lab weekly update: follow .claude/skills/weekly-update/SKILL.md." Nothing goes until you press Enter.
steps.notice: You can read it, edit it or delete it first. Pressing Enter starts the real update.
steps.risk: In this test the box stayed greyed out, because the test window was not signed in to Claude. In your app it unlocks once the conversation is ready.

steps.path: Frontier Lab, opened again after its page and data were rebuilt
steps.headline: Rebuilding the page or its data later never brings the card or a 'code changed' note back.
steps.changed: This permission is not tied to the page's code. A copy of the page was edited (page and data both), then opened again.
steps.notice: The weekly update can rewrite Frontier Lab every week and it still opens straight away.
steps.risk: A later rebuild could change the message the button writes without asking you again. You still see it in the chat box before you press Enter.

steps.path: Any page button that starts a conversation, such as Update now
steps.headline: Should the window show the page's message before you press Create Session?
steps.today: The window shows the project, model and permission switch. The message only appears in the chat box after Create Session, with the cursor at its end.
steps.problem: You choose the project and permissions before reading what you are about to run. A long message shows only its last lines, so its start is scrolled out of sight. Frontier Lab's message is one short line, so this matters for longer messages.
steps.proposal: Pick how a page's message should be shown before you send it.

options.label: Preview in window
pros: You read the whole message before you choose the project or press Create Session
Matches the card's promise that you see the message first
A long message scrolls inside the window, from its first line
cons: You see the message twice: once in the window, once in the chat box

options.label: Cursor at start
pros: Smallest change: the window looks the same
A long message in the chat box opens on its first line
cons: You still pick the project and permissions before seeing the message
Typing goes in at the start, not after the message as in a normal chat

options.label: Leave as is
pros: No more work, and nothing is ever sent before you press Enter
cons: The card's wording promises more than the window shows
Long messages open scrolled to their end
